title: GPU Servicing Tiers & Overprovision Credits Pilot
creator: Aisha Kumar
description:
Summary: Pilot a two-axis packaging experiment for Dedicated GPU customers: (1) introduce explicit 'Servicing Tiers' that guarantee different p99 latency and throughput lanes (baseline / premium / critical), and (2) offer optional 'Overprovision Credits' — a prepaid cushion customers can consume when autoscale or burst capacity is constrained.

Background: Current reserved GPU packages conflate capacity, priority, and burstability. Sales and Solutions teams ask for a simple, contract-friendly way to promise differentiated latency commitments without over-selling costly reserve capacity. Engineering has an autoscale proof-of-concept that supports preemption-aware lanes; legal asks for clear contract language around burst consumption and credit burn.

Goals:
- Create packaging that maps to measurable infra constructs (lane priorities + credit pool) so SRE can enforce fallthroughs.
- Keep unit economics sensible: pilots must demonstrate <=10% increase in infra cost per committed unit for Premium lane.
- Produce contract language and an annotated Enterprise SQ checklist for security/compliance impacts.
- Validate customer willingness to prepay for credits (target 20% conversion in pilot accounts).

Experiment sketch (A/B):
- Variant A: Tiered SLA product (Baseline / Premium / Critical) with fixed price multipliers and no prepaid credits; burst handled by best-effort preemption fallback.
- Variant B: Baseline tier + optional Overprovision Credit buckets (small/medium/large) that customers can buy; credits consumed when autoscale borrows capacity from burst pools; credits priced to reflect expected marginal infra cost + 30% margin.

Metrics / success criteria:
- Revenue signal: conversion rate for credits >= 15% across pilot accounts.
- Reliability: No increase in P99 failures for Baseline lane during pilot windows.
- Economics: Incremental cost per reserved-GPU (marginal infra) stays within modeled range; simulated billings vs actual infra consumption variance < 12%.
- Sales adoption: At least 3 enterprise pilots include the new tier in term sheets within 6 weeks.

Constraints & open questions:
- How do credits reconcile with current invoice model (usage-based + reserved delta)? Need Finance input.
- Billing edge cases: expired credits, pro-rata when downgrade mid-cycle.
- Security/compliance: overprovisioning must preserve VPC isolation and not leak capacity telemetry across tenants.

Deliverables:
1) Pricing model spreadsheet (unit economics & sensitivity analysis) with scenario runs.
2) Contract language snippets for term sheets and SOWs (billing + SLA).
3) Enterprise SQ addendum draft describing operational controls for credit consumption.
4) Telemetry dashboard spec and alerting thresholds for pilot.
5) Pilot onboarding doc and sales enablement one-pager.

Stakeholders: PM (Aisha Kumar), Solutions Eng (Priya Nair), SRE (Diego Morales), Finance (Marco Li), Legal (Hannah Schultz), Security (Omar Patel).
acceptance_criteria: 1) Pricing spreadsheet with at least 3 scenarios uploaded to Drive and signed off by Finance; 2) Contract snippets reviewed by Legal and stored in contracts repo; 3) Pilot telemetry dashboard created and test data ingested; 4) Two pilot customers committed to test Variant B; 5) Security checklist completed and no unresolved items listed.

2025-03-10 - PM note: Rebranded to 'Overprovision Credits' for now to match legal draft. Preparing two pilot proposals for enterprise accounts: AcmeHealth and VertoAI. Next steps: finalize pricing tiers and run spike to simulate cost variance for 30-day traffic patterns.
